pull.title: tracking: enforce server-side GPS update throttling
pull.body:
## Summary
- add a configurable server-side minimum interval for live GPS writes (`TRACKING_MIN_UPDATE_INTERVAL_MILLIS`, default 1000 ms)
- enforce the interval inside the existing row-locked tracking transaction so concurrent or modified clients cannot bypass it
- keep `receivedAt` tied to actual GPS samples when pickup changes the tracking phase, preserving stale-position semantics
- add focused unit coverage for first update, boundary timing, rejection, disable mode and invalid configuration
- document the security/operational invariant in the live-tracking architecture guide

## Why
The web client already uploads GPS roughly every 5 seconds, but client-side throttling is not a security boundary. Without a backend floor, a modified client can flood position writes and indirectly increase realtime/ETA work.

## Validation
GitHub-hosted CI is the source of truth for this branch. Do not merge until the backend/frontend/container checks are green.

discussion_comments.body:
CI follow-up: the runtime smoke was still receiving the production 1000 ms throttle because `TRACKING_MIN_UPDATE_INTERVAL_MILLIS` existed in Spring configuration but was missing from both `.env.example` and the API service environment in `compose.yaml`. That made the CI `sed` override a no-op and the second synthetic GPS update returned 429/4xx.

Fixed on this branch by exposing the variable in `.env.example` and passing it through Compose. Latest CI is running on `0d5a9d21f884f183c4a71fcef3b97556605da3a6`; leaving the PR unmerged until all checks are green.
